historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Antifolate antimetabolites

starting.description: Farber's interpretation of apparent leukemia acceleration after folate conjugates, experience with folate deficiency, and observed growth inhibition by a synthetic folate antagonist suggested testing more powerful antagonists. His 1947 report traces the earlier conjugate trials to mouse-tumor studies that Diamond later said could not be substantiated. These historical observations are not proof of a causal acceleration effect.

inspiration.description: The natural vitamin folate, interpreted clinical and physiological effects, and an observed synthetic folate antagonist's growth effects in experimental organisms supplied clues for the cancer program.

steps.description: Prior mouse reports prompted folate-conjugate trials; folate-related clinical observations and measured biological antagonism suggested testing folate antagonists against rapidly growing malignancies. An early pteroylaspartic-acid observation helped motivate stronger antagonists.
Chemists synthesized a potent 4-amino folate antagonist by 1947; aminopterin was tested in children with leukemia, with temporary improvements and important toxicity.

Amethopterin, later methotrexate, was developed and tested as another folate antagonist; Farber's 1949 abstract reports temporary remissions and toxicity with it. It is the N10-methyl analogue of aminopterin.

design.description: Chemists synthesized folate analogues and measured antagonistic activity. Aminopterin has an amino substitution in place of the pteridine oxygen, and methotrexate has an additional N10-methyl group; these are changes in active structure, not merely formulation. Clinical investigators deliberately tested the antagonists against leukemia following biological and clinical clues.

circumstances.description: The testing of folate antagonists in children with leukemia was a deliberate therapeutic investigation; this does not classify every earlier observation as planned or accidental.

limits: The documented founding sequence is the cytotoxic folate-antagonist lineage represented by methotrexate. Antibacterial DHFR inhibitors have a separate origin and are excluded.
Later immunomodulatory indications and the separate design histories of every later antifolate were not reconstructed; no separate from-scratch founding branch is established within this cohort.
conflicts: Kohn describes a 1948 report as spurring synthesis of aminopterin, but Seeger et al. published its synthesis in October 1947 and Farber et al. state that aminopterin was administered from November 1947; the retrospective chronology cannot be the initial trigger as stated (E12, E11, E7).

DeVita and Chu later call the apparent folate-related leukemia acceleration spurious; Farber described it as his interpretation. The later review does not identify evidence for its refutation in that sentence, so neither causality nor refutation is established here (E5, E9).
gaps: The 1947 and 1948 clinical reports and 1947 chemical report were accessed as indexed text without page-image confirmation or full local copies. The 1949 Farber report was abstract-only, and the 1949 Seeger chemistry report was located but not read.

The later evidentiary basis for calling folate-induced leukemia acceleration spurious, the complete chronology and motivation of individual chemists' analogue design, and a controlled human safety comparison were not established.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Apparent acceleration of leukemia after folate-conjugate treatment helped motivate testing folate antagonists.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: The uncontrolled deterioration is a reported inspiration, not proof that folate caused acceleration; animal testing also contributed.
